If he were to remain in the Fire forever, he would not seek relief, because beholding the Real, its impact upon him, his rescue and his ruin are [for him] but one [object of regard]. The vision of exclusive oneness has obliterated every veil, so that speaker and one addressed are one; the Real is addressing Himself through Himself.” On “When night covered him, he saw a star” (Q 6:76), al-Wāsiṭī says: “In his secret he looks to the Real, not to the star.”

pairs.ar: وقوله : وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ [ الأنعام : 98 ] ، قال الواسطي : مستقر فيه أنوار الذات على الأبد . وقوله : وَإِنْ تُطِعْ أَكْثَرَ مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ [ الأنعام : 116 ] ، قيل : من نظر إلى سوى الحق خاب وضل . وفي قوله تعالى : وَكَلَّمَهُ رَبُّهُ [ الأعراف : 143 ] ، سأل النظر إليه إذ رجع إلى حقيقته ، فرأى اللّه في كل منظور له ومبصر . وقوله : فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّى رَبُّهُ [ الأعراف : 143 ] ، قال الواسطي : وصل إلى الخلق من صفاته ونعوته على مقادير هم لا كلية الصفات ، كما أن التجلي لم يكن بكلية الذات .
pairs.en: On “It is He who brought you forth from a single soul; then there is a dwelling-place ...” (Q 6:98), al-Wāsiṭī says: “The lights of the Essence rest within it forever.” On “If you obey most of those on earth” (Q 6:116), it is said: “Whoever looks to anything other than the Real is disappointed and goes astray.” On “His Lord spoke to him” (Q 7:143): “He requested sight of Him when he returned to his own reality, and saw God in every object seen and contemplated.” On “When his Lord disclosed Himself” (Q 7:143), al-Wāsiṭī says: “What reached creatures of His attributes and descriptions was according to their measures, not the totality of the attributes, just as the self-disclosure was not through the totality of the Essence.”

editorial_note: The wording «وطئه» in the al-Fārisī quotation is uncertain; “its impact upon him” is provisional. The final claim explicitly distinguishes the measure of the receiver from exhaustive disclosure of the divine Essence; the passage is transmitted from al-Wāsiṭī, not yet al-Mahāʾimī’s independent metaphysical proof.

title: Existence and existentiation under two perspectives
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī quoting and discussing earlier authorities; follow explicit attribution in each paragraph

pairs.ar: وقوله : فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ . . . الآية [ الأنفال : 17 ] ، قال بعضهم : ما رميت ، ولكن رميت بسهم الجمع فغيبك عنك ، فرميت ولا سيّما الرّامين عنك ؛ لأن المباشرة منك ، والحقيقة لنا إذا لم نفرق . وفي قوله : وَلا تَعْمَلُونَ مِنْ عَمَلٍ إِلَّا كُنَّا عَلَيْكُمْ شُهُوداً [ يونس : 61 ] وقال بعضهم : من شهد شهوده إياه ؛ قطعه ذلك عن مشاهدة الأغيار أجمع . وفي قوله تعالى : وَأَنِ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ [ هود : 3 ] قال يوسف : واستغفار الأكابر من رؤية كل شيء سوى الحق .
pairs.en: On “You did not kill them ...” (Q 8:17), someone says: “You did not cast, but you cast with the arrow of gathering, so He hid you from yourself. You cast, yet [He displaced] the throwers from you [uncertain wording]: the immediate act is yours, while reality belongs to Us when We do not make a separation.” On “Nor do you perform an act without Our being witnesses over you” (Q 10:61), someone says: “Whoever witnesses His witnessing of him is thereby cut off from contemplating all others.” On “Ask your Lord's forgiveness” (Q 11:3), Yūsuf says: “The great ones ask forgiveness for seeing anything at all besides the Real.”

pairs.ar: وقوله : وَلِلَّهِ غَيْبُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُ الْأَمْرُ كُلُّهُ [ هود : 123 ] ، قال النهرجوري : ولا يطلع عليه إلا الأمناء . ثم قال : هم الذين لم يبق عليهم منهم حظ ، ولا لهم منهم مطالبة ، فكانوا بلا كون ، وشهدوا بلا شهود . ثم قال : فلا هم هم ، ولا هم لا هم ، فهم هم من حيث الوجود ، ولا هم من حيث الإيجاد . ثم قال : أخرجوا عن حدود التفرقة إلى عين الجمع ، فهم مجموعون في عين جمع الجمع .
pairs.en: On “To God belongs the unseen of the heavens and earth, and to Him the entire affair returns” (Q 11:123), al-Nahrajūrī says: “None gains access to it except the trustworthy.” Then: “They are those in whom nothing is left for themselves, who retain no claims on their own behalf; so they existed without [their own] being and witnessed without [their own] witnessing.” And: “They are neither themselves nor not themselves: they are themselves insofar as existence (*min ḥayth al-wujūd*) is considered, but not themselves insofar as the bringing-into-existence (*min ḥayth al-ījād*) is considered.” And: “They have been taken beyond the bounds of separation to the very reality of gathering, so that they are gathered in the very reality of the gathering of gatherings.”

pairs.ar: وفي قوله تعالى : وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ [ يوسف : 24 ] ، قال ابن عطاء : احتالت زليخا أن تري نفسها ليوسف ، فحجب اللّه نفسها عن يوسف بالبرهان العالي والحق الظاهر ، حتى لم يشهد في وقته غير الحق « 1 » . وفي قوله : أَ فَمَنْ هُوَ قائِمٌ عَلى كُلِّ نَفْسٍ [ الرعد : 33 ] ، قال الجنيد : باللّه قامت الأشياء ، وبه فنيت ، وبتجليه حسنت المحاسن ، وباستتاره قبحت وسمجت . وفي قوله تعالى : وَاعْبُدْ رَبَّكَ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَكَ الْيَقِينُ [ الحجر : 99 ] ، قال الواسطي : فتتحقق أنك لا تحس بغير الحق ، ولا ترى إلا الحق ، ولا تحادث إلا الحق .
pairs.en: On “She indeed desired him” (Q 12:24), Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says: “Zulaykhā contrived to display herself to Joseph, but God veiled her from him by the highest proof and the manifest Real, so that at that moment he witnessed nothing but the Real.” On “Is He who stands over every soul ...” (Q 13:33), al-Junayd says: “Through God things stood, through Him they perished, through His self-disclosure beauties became beautiful, and through His concealment they became ugly and repellent.” On “Worship your Lord until certainty comes to you” (Q 15:99), al-Wāsiṭī says: “You then realize that you sense nothing but the Real, see nothing but the Real, and converse with nothing but the Real.”

editorial_note: The contrast between *min ḥayth al-wujūd* and *min ḥayth al-ījād* is explicit. Its first speaker here is al-Nahrajūrī as transmitted through al-Sulamī. Treat it as a register distinction in reported language, not proof that the terms denote different independently existing objects. The longer story about Joseph in footnote 1 is editorial and omitted.

title: Moses, fanāʾ, and the measure of revelation
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī quoting and discussing earlier authorities; follow explicit attribution in each paragraph

pairs.ar: وفي قوله تعالى : فَلَمَّا أَتاها نُودِيَ يا مُوسى * إِنِّي أَنَا رَبُّكَ [ طه : 11 ، 12 ] ، قيل لموسى : كيف عرفت أن النداء هو نداء الحق ؟ فقال : أفناني وشملني ، فكان كل شعرة مني ، كان مخاطبا بنداء من جميع الجهات ، وكأنها تعبر عن نفسها بجواب ، ولما شملتني أنوار الهيبة ، وأحاطت لي أنوار العزة والجبروت ؛ علمت أنه ليس لأحد أن يخبر عن نفسه باللفظين جميعا متتابعا إلا الحق .
pairs.en: On “When he came to it, he was called: O Moses! Truly I am your Lord” (Q 20:11–12), Moses was asked: “How did you know that the call was the call of the Real?” He replied: “It effaced me and encompassed me; every hair upon me became an addressee of a call coming from every direction, as though each hair expressed an answer. When the lights of awe enveloped me and the lights of might and dominion surrounded me, I knew that no one could speak of himself using those two successive expressions [‘I’ and ‘your Lord’] except the Real.”

pairs.ar: قال : وكان هو محل الفناء ، فقلت أنت ، أنت لم تزل ، وليس لموسى معك مقام ، ولا له جرأة على الكلام ؛ إلا أن تبقيه ببقائك تنعته بنعوتك ، فتكون أنت المخاطب والمخاطب جميعا . قال : لا يحمل خطابي غيري ولا يجيبني سواي ، أنا المتكلم والمكلم وأنت في الوسط شبح يقع بك محل الخطاب . وفي قوله : وَوَجَدَ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ [ النور : 39 ] ، قال ابن عطاء : ما وجد الخلق سوى الحق « 1 » .
pairs.en: He said: “That was the place of effacement, and I said: ‘You! You have never ceased to be; Moses has no standing with You and no boldness to speak, unless You preserve him through Your abiding and characterize him with Your attributes; then You are both the one addressing and the one addressed.’” He [the quoted speaker] said: “‘No one carries My speech but I, and none answers Me but I. I am speaker and one spoken to; you are a shadowy figure in between, serving as the place of address.’” On “He found God with him” (Q 24:39), Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says: “Creatures found nothing but the Real.”

pairs.ar: وفي قوله تعالى : سَنُرِيهِمْ آياتِنا فِي الْآفاقِ [ فصلت : 53 ] ، قال الخطمي : لا يزال العبد يرتقي من حال إلى حال ؛ حتى يبلغ الأحوال السنيّة العالية ، ويرى اللّه قائما بالأشياء فانية في رؤية الحق ، ويتيقن أن القديم إذا قورن بالحادث لا يثبت له أثر ، وإن جل قدره وعظم خطره .
pairs.en: On “We shall show them Our signs on the horizons” (Q 41:53), al-Khaṭmī says: “A servant continues to rise from one state to another until he reaches elevated and lofty states, and sees God sustaining things, which vanish in the witnessing of the Real. He becomes certain that when the eternal is compared with the temporally originated, the latter retains no effect [in that regard], however great its worth and importance.”

pairs.ar: وهو معنى قوله : آياتِنا فِي الْآفاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ [ فصلت : 53 ] ، وهو النظر إلى الكون يشاهد الحق ، ثم النظر إلى الحق بالفناء عن الكون ، وهو أن تصير النعوت نعتا واحدا ولا يشهد إلا حقّا صرفا . وسئل أبو عثمان عمن يقول بالشاهد ، وقال : لا أنكر القول لمن يشهد الأشياء كلها شيئا واحدا .
pairs.en: This is the meaning of “Our signs on the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that He is the Real” (Q 41:53): first contemplating the cosmos while witnessing the Real, then contemplating the Real while being effaced from the cosmos, when the many attributes become one attribute and one witnesses nothing but the pure Real. Abū ʿUthmān was asked about someone who speaks of *the witnessed one* [*al-shāhid*, reading/context uncertain]. He answered: “I do not reject the assertion of someone who witnesses all things as one thing.”

editorial_note: The source's report about Moses is an esoteric transmitted narrative, not a verified prophetic ḥadīth. The printed editor cites Ibn ʿAjība in footnote 1; this is excluded from al-Mahāʾimī’s main text. The subject of *fanāʾ* must be kept distinct from a claim of hypostatic fusion.

title: The lights of creation and the collapse of separate agency
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī quoting and discussing earlier authorities; follow explicit attribution in each paragraph

pairs.ar: قال الواسطي : ظهر في كل شيء بما أظهر منه ، وإظهاره الأشياء ظهوره بها ، فإذا فتشتها لا تجد غير اللّه ، ولذلك قال صلى اللّه عليه وسلّم : « أصدق كلمة قالها لبيد : ألا كل شيء ما خلا اللّه باطل » « 1 » . وفي قوله تعالى أَلا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَصِيرُ الْأُمُورُ [ الشورى : 3 ] ، قال : لأن منه مبدأ كل شيء ، وإليه منتهى كل شيء ، فما كان منه وله فهو الساعة به . وفي قوله تعالى : وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ [ ق : 16 ] ، ومن تحقق ذلك لعامر بن قيس حين قال : ما نظرت شيئا إلا ورأيت اللّه أقرب إلىّ منه .
pairs.en: Al-Wāsiṭī said: “He manifested Himself in every thing by what He displayed through it, and His displaying things is His manifestation through them. Examine them closely and you will find none but God. This is why the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: ‘The truest saying spoken by Labīd is: Everything apart from God is vain.’” On “Surely to God all affairs return” (Q 42:53; the source identifies Q 42:3, apparently in error), he says: “For everything's beginning is from Him and its end goes back to Him; what is from Him and for Him is, in the present instant, through Him.” On “We are nearer to him” (Q 50:16), ʿĀmir ibn Qays expressed the realization when he said: “I have never looked at a thing without seeing God nearer to me than that thing.”

pairs.ar: وفي قوله تعالى : هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْباطِنُ [ الحديد : 3 ] ، قال جعفر الصادق رضي اللّه عنه : فسقطت هذه المعاني وبقي هو « 2 » . وعن الشبلي : الأشياء ساقطة بأنه أول ، آخر ، ظاهر ، باطن ، إلى غير ذلك من المواضع . ومنها ما قال الشيخ الكامل المحقق أبو طالب المكي ، في كتابه « قوت القلوب » ، في ذكر وصف الزاهد وفضل الزهد : وروينا عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى : جَمِيعاً مِنْهُ [ الجاثية : 13 ] ، قال : في كل حرف اسم من أسمائه تعالى ، فكان اسم كل شيء عين اسمه ، كما أن فعل كل عين فعله .
pairs.en: On “He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward” (Q 57:3), Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq said: “These meanings fell away, and He alone remained.” From al-Shiblī: “Things fall away because He is First, Last, Outward and Inward.” There are many similar places. Another authority is the accomplished and verifying shaykh Abū Ṭālib al-Makkī, who says in *Qūt al-qulūb*, in the discussion of the ascetic and the excellence of renunciation: “We have related from Ibn ʿAbbās on the words ‘all of it from Him’ (Q 45:13): ‘In every letter is one of His names, exalted is He; thus the name of every thing is identical with His name, just as the act of every entity is identical with His act.’”

pairs.ar: ثم ذكر في فصل آخر : قيل لبعض العارفين هل تأسف الولي على غير اللّه ؟ فقال : وهل يرى غير اللّه فيأسف عليه . ثم قال في شرح مقام التوحيد : كل وصف أحكام المتوكلين حين نظر الولي إلى مولاه الذي تولاه فرآه في كل شيء . ثم قال : إذا كملت مشاهدته وقام بحق شهادته ؛ غيّبت تلك المشاهدة برؤية القيومية وجود الخلقية مع اللّه ، فلم يرها دونه ، قامت له القيومية بنصبه من الملك لما تفرغ قلب لمعاينة الملك ، وهذا من عين اليقين فوق علمه ؛ لأن الحق المبين هو الأول والآخر كما
pairs.en: Elsewhere he relates that a knower was asked: “Does a friend of God grieve for anything other than God?” He answered: “Does he see anything other than God, that he might grieve for it?” In his explanation of the station of unification, he describes the conditions of those who trust in God as the friend turns to his protecting Lord and sees Him in everything. Then: “When his witnessing is perfected and he fulfills the duty of bearing witness, that witnessing—by the vision of God's self-subsistence—renders invisible the existence of creatures *alongside* God. He does not see them apart from Him. The divine self-subsistence stands before him ... when the heart is entirely free to behold the King. This belongs to the eye of certainty, beyond his [discursive] knowledge, because the manifest Real is First and Last, just as ...” [Continued on p. 32. The middle of the Arabic period is defective or severely compressed.]

editorial_note: The verse «ألا إلى الله تصير الأمور» is Q 42:53, not 42:3. «وجود الخلقية مع الله» explicitly contains the preposition *maʿa*; it speaks of the apparent “alongside” in witnessing, not simply created dependence. The long Abū Ṭālib al-Makkī passage has a corrupt clause (قام له القيومية بنصبه من الملك...) needing independent comparison with *Qūt al-qulūb*.

title: Causes, intermediaries, and differing scriptural attributions
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī quoting and discussing earlier authorities; follow explicit attribution in each paragraph

pairs.ar: هو الظاهر والباطن . ثم قال : وبعض أشياخنا إذا سئل عن التوكل ؛ أجاب عنه بعين الحقيقة ، فيقول : هو أن تكون مع الحق ، كما لم تكن ، فإن الحق الآن كما لم يزل . ثم قال : يا مسكين كان ولم تكن ، ويكون ولا تكون ، فلمّا كنت اليوم ، قلت أنا وأنا ، كن فيما أنت الآن كما لم تكن ، فاليوم كما كان .
pairs.en: ... He is the Outward and the Inward. Then he says: “When certain of our shaykhs were asked about trust in God, they answered from the very reality of the matter: ‘It is to be with the Real as though you had never been, for the Real is now as He always was.’” Then: “Poor soul! He existed when you were not; He will exist when you will not. When today you came to be, you said, ‘I, I!’ Be now, in your present existence, as though you were not, for today remains as it always was.”

pairs.ar: ثم قال في ذكر إثبات الأسباب والأوساط : فالمتوكل لا يرى إلا اللّه ، ووصفه وفعله وحكمه ، ففعله ظاهر ، ووصفه باطن ، واللّه الظاهر الباطن ، وحكمه هو الرسم ، واللّه الحاكم الراسم ، ثم قال : فإن اللّه قد أظهر أسبابا وأثبت نفسه فيها ، فقال : قُلْ يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ مَلَكُ الْمَوْتِ [ السجدة : 11 ] ، ثم رفعه وأظهر نفسه فقال : اللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى الْأَنْفُسَ [ الزمر : 42 ] ، وكذلك قال في التفصيل : إِنَّهُمُ اتَّخَذُوا الشَّياطِينَ أَوْلِياءَ [ الأعراف : 30 ] ، وقال في التوحيد : إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا الشَّياطِينَ أَوْلِياءَ [ الأعراف : 27 ] ، وكما قال في المتشابه : وَأَضَلَّهُمُ السَّامِرِيُّ [ طه : 85 ] ، وقال في المحكم : إِلَّا فِتْنَتُكَ تُضِلُّ بِها مَنْ تَشاءُ وَتَهْدِي مَنْ تَشاءُ [ الأعراف : 155 ] ، ثم قال : وكذلك قيل عن اللّه تبارك وتعالى : أنا الدليل على نفسي ، لا دليل أدل علي مني .
pairs.en: Then, concerning the affirmation of causes and intermediaries: “The one who trusts in God sees nothing but God, His attribute, His act, and His command. His act is outward, His attribute inward; God is the Outward and the Inward. His command is the inscribed trace, and God is the One who commands and inscribes.” Then: “God has brought causes into appearance and established Himself [as the true agent] within them. Thus He says, ‘Say: the Angel of Death will take you’ (Q 32:11); then He rises beyond that [secondary attribution] and makes Himself manifest: ‘God takes souls’ (Q 39:42). Likewise, in a differentiated account He says, ‘They took the devils as protectors’ (Q 7:30), while under the aspect of unification He says, ‘We made the devils protectors’ (Q 7:27). In one formulation He says, ‘The Sāmirī led them astray’ (Q 20:85); in another, ‘It is nothing but Your trial; You lead astray by it whomever You will and guide whomever You will’ (Q 7:155).” Then: “It is likewise related of God, blessed and exalted: ‘I am My own proof; no proof points to Me more surely than I.’”

pairs.ar: ثم قال في ذكر حكم المتوكل في مزيد آخر من الهدى والبيان . وقال بعض العارفين : إذا رأيت الأشياء كلها كشيء واحد ، من معدن واحد ، بعين واحدة ؛ أريت ما لم تر قبل ذلك ، وسمعت ما لم تسمع وفهمت ما لم يفهم الخلق . ثم قال في ذكر أحكام المحبة ووصف أهلها : وتقلب محبة على هوى العبد حتى محبة اللّه هي محبة العبد من كل شيء ، فهو محب للّه حقا ، كما أنه مؤمن به حقا عن مشاهدة اليقين ؛ الذي يغلب رؤيته على رؤية الخلق فيشهده في كل شيء ، ويكون واحدا به دون كل شيء ؛ إذ قد تجلى ، فمن أيقن بكل شيء .
pairs.en: Then, in a further account of the one who trusts in God and of guidance and clarification, a knower says: “When you see all things as though they were one thing, from one mine and with one eye, you will be shown what you had never seen before, hear what you had never heard, and understand what people had not understood.” In discussing love and its possessors, [Abū Ṭālib] continues: “Love ... [source syntactically uncertain] until love of God becomes the servant's love in relation to everything. Then he loves God truly just as he believes in Him truly, through the vision of certainty that makes his vision [of God] prevail over his vision of creatures: he witnesses Him in everything and is one through Him without anything else, for He has disclosed Himself ...” [Final wording of the passage remains defective.]

pairs.ar: ثم قال : وما قال التوحيد إلا الواحد ، وما قال اللّه إلا اللّه ، ثم قال : لقد بطنت . . إلى آخره . ثم قال في ذكر مخاوف المحبين ومقاماتهم في الخوف : لقد ظهرت لمن أفنيت بعد فنائه * فكان بلا كون لأنّك كنته قيل قبله :
pairs.en: Then: “None uttered unification but the One; none uttered ‘God’ but God.” Next he says: “You have been inward ...” [and so forth]. In speaking of the fears of lovers and their stations of fear, he cites: “You became manifest to him whom You had effaced, after his effacement; / so he was without a being of his own, because You were his being.” The following verse, he says, had been recited before it [see p. 33].

editorial_note: The pair 32:11 / 39:42 gives explicitly differentiated versus comprehensive attribution of a single act, not a straightforward claim that angels are unreal. «أثبت نفسه فيها» is not to be silently reinterpreted as a spatial indwelling. An earlier reading quoted «تقلّب محبة» is textually uncertain.

title: Divine proximity and the beginning of al-Anṣārī’s testimonies
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī quoting and discussing earlier authorities; follow explicit attribution in each paragraph

pairs.ar: لقد بطنت ولا تخفى على أحد * إلّا على أكمه لا يعرف القمرا ثم قال : لقد ظهرت فما تخفى على أحد * إلّا على أكمه لا يعرف القمرا لقد بطنت فما أظهرت محتجبا * وكيف يعرف من بالعرف استترا فصرت أعجب ما عانيت مجتهدا * لأننّي حاجب استطلع الخبرا
pairs.en: “You have been hidden, yet are hidden from no one / except a blind man who cannot recognize the moon.” Then he says: “You have become manifest, hidden from no one / except a blind man who cannot recognize the moon. / You have remained inward, while I have disclosed no veiled one; / how can he be known who was veiled by the very means of knowing? / I became the strangest thing I encountered in my striving, / for I myself am a veil that tries to discover the news.” [The poem's subject shifts and the wording of its second and third lines calls for collation.]

pairs.ar: ثم قال : هو الناظر والمنظور ، والسامع والمسموع ، وهو الشاهد والمشهود ، وهو الواجد والموجود ، كما قال بعض المحبين : ليس في القلب والعيان جميعا * موضع فارغ لغير الحبيب هو سقمي وصحّتي وشفائي * وبه العيش ما حييت بطيب
pairs.en: Then: “He is the seer and what is seen, the hearer and what is heard; He is the witness and the witnessed, the finder and what is found.” As a lover says: “Neither within the heart nor in what the eye beholds / is there any vacant space for anything but the Beloved. / He is my illness, my health, my cure; / through Him life is sweet so long as I live.”

pairs.ar: ثم قال في شرح دعائم الإسلام ، وفرض التوحيد : هو اعتقاد القلب أن اللّه تعالى واحد لا من عدد ، إلى أن قال : آخر في أوليته ، أول في آخريته ، وأن أسماءه وصفاته وأنواره غير مخلوقة ولا منفصلة عنه ، وأنه أمام كل شيء ، ووراء كل شيء ، وفوق كل شيء ، ومع كل شيء ، وأقرب إلى كل شيء من نفس الشيء ، وأنه مع ذلك غير محل للأشياء ، وأن الأشياء ليست محلا له ، إلى غير ذلك من المواضع .
pairs.en: Then, explaining the pillars of Islam and the obligation of divine unity: “It is the heart's conviction that God, exalted is He, is one—not as a unit in a number.” Farther on: “He is Last in His Firstness and First in His Lastness; His names, attributes and lights are neither created nor separate from Him. He is before everything, behind everything, above everything, with everything, and closer to everything than the thing is to itself; yet He is not a locus in which things inhere, nor are things loci in which He inheres.” There are further statements of this kind.

pairs.ar: وأقول : يناسبه ما روى الواحدي والبغوي ، عن وهب بن منبه : « نودي من الشجرة ؛ قيل يا موسى ، فأجاب سريعا ما يدرى من دعاه . فقال : إني أسمع صوتك ولا أرى مكانك ، فأين أنت ؟ فقال : أنا فوقك ، ومعك ، وأمامك ، وخلفك ، وأقرب إليك من نفسك ، فعلم أن ذلك لا ينبغي إلا للّه عز وجل ، فأيقن به » « 1 » . ومنها ما قال شيخ الإسلام أبو إسماعيل عبد اللّه الأنصاري ، في كتابه « منازل السائرين » « 2 » : ولا يتم مقام التوبة إلا بالانتهاء من التوبة مما دون الحق ، ثم رؤية علة تلك التوبة ، ثم توبة من رؤية تلك العلة ، وفرار خاصة الخاصة مما دون الحق إلى الحق ، ثم من شهود الفرار إلى الحق ، ثم الفرار من الفرار إلى الحق ، وفي باب السماع وسماع الخاصة ثلاثة
pairs.en: **Al-Mahāʾimī adds:** “I say: What al-Wāḥidī and al-Baghawī relate from Wahb ibn Munabbih is fitting here: ‘A call came from the tree: “O Moses!” He answered quickly without knowing who had called him. He said: “I hear Your voice but do not see Your place. Where are You?” He answered: “I am above you, with you, before you, behind you, and nearer to you than your own self.” Moses knew that such a thing befitted none but God, mighty and glorious, and became certain of Him.’” Among the testimonies is also that of the Shaykh of Islam Abū Ismāʿīl ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī in *Manāzil al-sāʾirīn*: “The station of repentance is not complete until one has ceased repenting merely of what is below the Real, then has perceived the defect in that repentance, then repented of perceiving that defect. The flight of the elect of the elect is first from what is beneath the Real to the Real, then from witnessing the flight to the Real, and finally from flight itself to the Real.” In the chapter on spiritual audition, the audition of the elect consists of three ... [continued on p. 34].

editorial_note: The words after «وأقول» are al-Mahāʾimī’s direct editorial intervention; his account of Wahb ibn Munabbih is a cited report and has not been established as authentic ḥadīth. The insistence on no literal *ḥulūl* (God as substrate and creatures as divine substrate) is explicit in the cited *Qūt* formulation.

title: Differentiated spiritual stations in al-Anṣārī
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī quoting and discussing earlier authorities; follow explicit attribution in each paragraph

pairs.ar: أشياء : شهود المقصود في كل أمر ، والوقوف على الغاية في كل همس ، والخلاص من التلذذ بالتفرق ، وسماع خاصة الخاصة سماع يغسل العلل عن الكشف ، ويصل الأبد بالأزل ، ويرد النهايات إلى الأول . وفي باب المراقبة : والدرجة الثالثة مراقبة الأزل بمطالعة عين السبق ؛ استقبالا لعلم التوحيد ، ومراقبة ظهور إشارات الأزل على إيحائين الأبد ومراقبة الخلاص من ربطة المراقبة ، فإن مراقبته تقيده برسمه ، فإذا فني رسمه فني قيده ، والرابطة هي القيد . وفي باب الشكر : والدرجة الثالثة ألا يشهد العبد إلا المنعم .
pairs.en: ... matters: “to witness the intended Object in every affair, to stand upon the ultimate end in every whisper, and to be delivered from taking pleasure in differentiation.” The audition of the elect of the elect is “an audition that washes impediments away from unveiling, joins everlasting duration with eternity without beginning, and returns endings to the First.” In the chapter on watchfulness (*murāqaba*), the third degree is “to be watchful of pre-eternity by contemplating the very reality of precedence, welcoming the knowledge of divine unity; to watch for the manifestation of the signs of pre-eternity upon [the allusions / intimations] of post-eternity; and to be free of the bond of watchfulness. One's watchfulness binds one by the trace of one's self; once that trace is annihilated, the bond disappears; the attachment itself is the bond.” In the chapter on gratitude, the third degree is that “the servant witnesses none but the Giver of blessings.”

pairs.ar: ثم قال : وإذا شهد المنعم معبوده استعظم منه النعمة ، وإذا شهده حبّا استحلى منه الشدة ، وإذا شهده تفريدا لم يشهد منه نعمة ولا شدة . وفي باب المشاهدة : والدرجة الثالثة : مشاهدة جمع تجذب إلى عين الجمع ، مالكة لصحة الورود ، راكبة بحر الوجود في باب البقاء ، وبقاء ما لم يزل حقّا بإسقاط ما لم يكن محوا ، أي بقاء الحق بإسقاط ما لم يكن موجودا ، حتى يمحو بالفناء فيه .
pairs.en: Then: “When he witnesses the Giver of blessings as his Worshipped One, he regards the gift as great; when he witnesses Him in love, he finds hardship sweet; when he witnesses Him in exclusive unification, he no longer witnesses either blessing or hardship as coming from Him.” In the chapter on direct witnessing, the third degree is “a witnessing of gathering which draws one into the very reality of gathering, possessing soundness of arrival and riding the sea of being.” In the chapter on subsistence: “Subsistence is the subsistence of what has eternally been Real, through the obliteration and dismissal of what never existed [in its own right]”—that is, the subsistence of the Real once what was not independently existent is dismissed, until it is obliterated through annihilation in Him.

pairs.ar: وفي باب الجمع : الجمع ما أسقط التفرقة ، وقطع الإشارة ، وشخص عن الماء والطين ؛ بعد صحة التمكين ، والبراءة من التلوين ، والخلاص من شهود الثنوية ، والتنافي من إحساس الاعتدال ، والتنافي من شهود شهودها ، وأما جمع الوجود فهو تلاشى نهاية الاتصال في عين الوجود محقّا ، وأما جمع العين ؛ فهو تلاشي كل ما تقله الإشارة في ذات الحق حقّا ، والجمع غاية مقامات السالكين ، وهو طرف بحر التوحيد .
pairs.en: In the chapter on gathering (*jamʿ*): “Gathering is that which casts down differentiation, severs pointing and indication, and departs from water and clay, after a firm establishment, freedom from changes of spiritual coloration and release from witnessing duality, [together with] removal of the feeling of equilibrium and even of witnessing its own witnessing.” As for *the gathering of being* (*jamʿ al-wujūd*), it is “the dissolution of the utmost limit of connection into the very reality of being, in complete realization”; *the gathering of the entity* (*jamʿ al-ʿayn*) is “the dissolution into the Essence of the Real of everything that indication could encompass.” Gathering is the utmost reach of the travellers' stations, and the brink of the sea of divine unity.

pairs.ar: وقال في باب التوحيد : والذي يشار به إليه على ألسن المشيرين أنه إسقاط الحدث ، وإثبات القدم ، قطب مدار الإشارة إلى هذا الطريق ، وأنه علة لا بد من إسقاطه . ثم قال : فإن التوحيد فوق ما يشير إليه مكون أو يتعاطاه حين أو يقله سبب . قال الشيخ الأنصاري : وقد أجبت في سالف الزمان سائلا - سألني عن توحيد الصوفية - بهذه القوافي الثلاث : ما وحّد الواحد من واحد * إذ كلّ من وحّده جاحد توحيد من ينطق عن نعته * عارية أبطلها الواحد توحيد إيّاه توحيده * ونعت من ينعته لاحد
pairs.en: In the chapter on divine unity: “The expression to which those who indicate point—casting off temporal origination and affirming beginninglessness—is the pivot around which indication turns on this path; yet it is itself a defect that must be cast aside.” Then: “Divine unity is beyond whatever any originated thing indicates, any occasion undertakes, or any cause bears.” Shaykh al-Anṣārī said: “Long ago I answered a questioner about the unity professed by the Sufis with these three rhyming verses: ‘No one has ever unified the One; / for whoever unifies Him thereby denies Him. / The unification voiced by one who speaks of His qualities / is a borrowed thing annulled by the One. / His unification is His own unifying of Himself; / the description given by one who describes Him is a departure [from the truth].’”

editorial_note: The language of “no one unifies the One” is an argument against regarding the servant as the *originating source* of divine unity. It must not be conflated with denial that the servant makes a true confession of tawḥīd. Several terms in the audition and gathering passage look corrupt, including «إيحائين» and «التنافي من إحساس الاعتدال»; translate provisionally pending a direct *Manāzil* collation.

title: Al-Kalābādhī: how opposed descriptions can designate a single state
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī quoting and discussing earlier authorities; follow explicit attribution in each paragraph

pairs.ar: إلى غير ذلك من المواضع . ومنها ما قال الشيخ أبو بكر الكلاباذي البخاري ، في كتاب « التعرف » في بحث المعرفة : أجمعوا على أن الدليل على اللّه عزّ وجل هو اللّه وحده . ثم نقل الثوري وابن عطاء والجنيد ، عن محمد بن واسع : ما رأيت شيئا إلا ورأيت اللّه فيه . وعن غيره : ما رأيت شيئا إلا ورأيت اللّه قبله . وعن الجنيد : أنه العارف والمعروف ، ومعناه أنك جاهل به من حيث أنت ؛ وإنما عرفته من حيث هو هو .
pairs.en: There are other such passages. Another authority is Shaykh Abū Bakr al-Kalābādhī of Bukhara, who says in *al-Taʿarruf*, in the discussion of knowledge: “They agree that God, exalted and majestic, is the sole proof of God.” He then transmits through al-Thawrī, Ibn ʿAṭāʾ and al-Junayd from Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ: “I never saw a thing without seeing God in it.” Another says: “I never saw a thing without seeing God before it.” From al-Junayd: “He is both knower and known.” This means that insofar as you are yourself, you do not know Him; rather, you have known Him insofar as He is He.

pairs.ar: ثم نقل في بحث الاتصال ، عن ابن عمر : كنا نتراءى اللّه في ذلك المكان ، يعني في الطواف على ما فسره ، هو بحث التجلي والاستتار .
pairs.en: Then, in the discussion of contact or connection (*ittiṣāl*), he relates from Ibn ʿUmar: “We used to behold God together in that place”—meaning, as [the author] explains, during the circumambulation. This belongs to the discussion of self-disclosure and concealment.

pairs.ar: ثم قال في بحث الفناء والبقاء : ومنهم من جعل هذه الأحوال كلها حالا واحدا - وإن اختلفت عباراتها ، فجعل الفناء بقاء والجمع تفرقة ، وكذلك الغيبة والشهود والشكر والصحو ، وذلك أن الفاني باق بما للحق ، فان عمّا له ، والثاني مجموع ؛ لأنه لا يشهد إلا الحق ، والمجموع مفارق ؛ لأنه لا يشهد إياه ولا الخلق ، وهو باق لدوامه مع الحق ، وهو جامع به ، وهو فان عما سواه ، مفارق لهم ، وهو غائب سكران لزوال التمييز عنه ، ومعنى زوال التمييز : هو ما قلناه بين الآلام والملاذ ، أو أن الأشياء تتوحد له ، فلا يشهد مخالفة ؛ إذ لا يصرفه الحق إلا في موافقاته ؛ وإنما يميز بين الشيئين وغيره ، فإذا صارت الأشياء شيئا واحدا سقط التمييز .
pairs.en: Then, in the discussion of annihilation (*fanāʾ*) and subsistence (*baqāʾ*): “Some have regarded all these states as a single state despite the difference in their expressions, and have made annihilation subsistence and gathering separation; likewise absence and witnessing, intoxication and sobriety [the transcription reads *shukr*, ‘gratitude’, rather than *sukr*, ‘intoxication’, requiring collation]. This is because one who is annihilated subsists in what belongs to the Real and is annihilated from what belongs to himself. Again, he is gathered because he witnesses only the Real; yet the gathered person is separate because he witnesses neither himself nor creation. He subsists because he remains with the Real, is gathered through Him, and annihilated from all else and separated from them. He is absent and intoxicated because discernment has disappeared from him. The disappearance of discernment means what we have said concerning pains and pleasures; or else things become united for him, so he does not witness contrariety, since the Real directs him only according to what accords with Him. Discernment distinguishes one thing from another, but when things become one thing, discernment falls away.”

pairs.ar: ثم قال في بحث التوحيد : ونصيبه من الحق وجود الحق ، وهو فيه ما سور فليس له متقدم ولا متأخر . ثم قال في صفة العارف : سئل الحسن بن علي - رضي اللّه عنهما : متى يكون العارف شهد الحق ؟ قال : إذا بدأ الشاهد ، وفني الشواهد ، وذهب الحواس ، واضمحل الإخلاص . ومعنى فناء الشواهد : سقوط رؤية الخلق عنك بمعنى الضر والنفع والذم والمدح ، وذهاب الحواس هو معنى قوله : « فبي ينطق وبي يبصر . . . إلى آخره » ، إلى غير ذلك من المواضع . ومنها ما قال الفاضل المحقق السيد شمس الدين السمرقندي ، في خاتمة شرح
pairs.en: Then, in the discussion of divine unity: “The portion of the servant granted from the Real is the being of the Real; [the next words, *wa-huwa fīhi mā sūr*, are obscure], for He has neither one preceding Him nor one following Him.” Then, describing the knower: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, may God be pleased with them both, was asked: “When does a knower witness the Real?” He said: “When the Witness appears, the witnesses vanish, the senses depart, and even sincerity fades away.” The annihilation of the witnesses means that your regard for creatures disappears insofar as harm, benefit, blame and praise are concerned. The departure of the senses is the meaning of His saying, “Through Me he speaks and through Me he sees ...” [and so forth]. There are many similar places. And there is what the learned verifier Sayyid Shams al-Dīn al-Samarqandī says in the conclusion to his commentary ... [continued on p. 36].

editorial_note: This is one of the strongest explicit witnesses to non-univocal state language: Kalābādhī reports different names for a state and explains what each highlights. The Arabic printed «الشكر» beside «الصحو», but “intoxication and sobriety” would normally be «السكر والصحو»; no emendation has been made to the copied Arabic. «ما سور» and the final *shāhid/shawāhid* passage require collation. The expression about acts of hearing/speaking is not directly an accurately verified text of a divine ḥadīth here.

title: Al-Samarqandī and al-Bayḍāwī on dependence and ascent
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī quoting and discussing earlier authorities; follow explicit attribution in each paragraph

pairs.ar: صحائفه : أحوال الناس منحصرة في ثلاثة أقسام : الاشتغال بالحق عن الغير ، والاشتغال بالحق مع الغير ، والاشتغال بالغير عن الحق . ثم قال : والثاني عند أهل الطريقة والحقيقة شرك ، والثالث كفر ، والأول فيه السعادة الكلية والبهجة الحقيقية في الأخرى والأولى ؛ فَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِالطَّاغُوتِ وَيُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدِ اسْتَمْسَكَ بِالْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقى لَا انْفِصامَ لَها [ البقرة : 256 ] .
pairs.en: ... on his *Ṣaḥāʾif*: “The conditions of people fall into three classes: occupation with the Real to the exclusion of anything else; occupation with the Real along with something else; and occupation with something else to the exclusion of the Real.” Then: “For the people of the path and of realization, the second is [a subtle form of] association; the third is unbelief; the first yields complete felicity and genuine joy in this world and the next: ‘Whoever rejects false objects of worship and believes in God has grasped the firmest handhold that never breaks’ (Q 2:256).”

pairs.ar: ومنها ما قال الفاضل المحقق القاضي ناصر الدين البيضاوي ، في أنوار التنزيل ، في تفسير قوله تعالى : فَأَيْنَما تُوَلُّوا فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ اللَّهِ [ البقرة : 115 ] ، أي : فثم ذاته . ثم قال : إن اللّه بإحاطته بالأشياء واسع عليم . وفي قوله تعالى : وَيَبْقى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ [ الرحمن : 27 ] ، ولو استقريت جهات الموجودات ، وتصفحت وجودها ؛ وجدتها بأسرها فانية في حد ذاتها إلا وجه اللّه ، أي : الوجه الذي يلي جهته .
pairs.en: Among these also is the learned verifier, Judge Nāṣir al-Dīn al-Bayḍāwī. In *Anwār al-tanzīl*, on “Wherever you turn, there is the Face of God” (Q 2:115), he glosses: “That is, His Essence is there.” Then: “By His encompassing of things God is All-Embracing, All-Knowing.” On “The Face of your Lord shall remain” (Q 55:27): “If you examined the directions or aspects of existents and considered their existence, you would find all of them perishing in themselves apart from the Face of God, that is, the aspect turned toward Him.”

pairs.ar: وقال في شرح المصابيح ، في باب الذكر ، في قوله صلى اللّه عليه وسلم عن اللّه عزّ وجل : « لا يزال العبد يتقرب إلي بالنوافل . . . إلى آخره » « 1 » . وإن العبد لا يزال يتقرب إلى اللّه تعالى بأنواع الطاعات وأصناف الرياضات ، ويترقى من مقام إلى آخر أعلى منه ؛ حتى يحبه اللّه سبحانه وتعالى ، فيجعله مستغرقا بملاحظة جناب قدسه ، بحيث ما لاحظ شيئا إلا لاحظ ربه ، فما التفت لفت ، وحابس ومحبوس ، وصانع ومصنوع ، فاعل ومفعول ؛ إلا رأى اللّه ، وهو آخر درجات السالكين ، وأول درجات الواصلين ، فيكون بهذا الاعتبار سمعه وبصره .
pairs.en: In his commentary on *al-Maṣābīḥ*, in the section on remembrance, concerning the divine saying reported by the Prophet, peace be upon him, “My servant continues to approach Me through supererogatory acts ...”: “A servant continues drawing near to God through many kinds of obedience and spiritual discipline, rising from one station to another, higher station, until God, exalted is He, loves him. He then immerses him in contemplation of the precinct of His holiness, so that he never attends to anything without attending to his Lord. Whenever he turns toward someone turning and someone turned toward, a captor and captive, maker and made, agent and patient, he sees God. This is the last degree of the travellers and the first degree of those who have arrived. Under *this consideration*, therefore, God becomes his hearing and his sight.”

pairs.ar: ثم قال في باب أسماء اللّه تعالى ، في شرح اسم اللّه : وكل ممكن فإنه لا وجود له ، بل وجوده من الجهة التي يلي الواجب تعالى ، وإليه أشار حيث قال : ألا كل شيء ما خلا اللّه باطل . وفي شرح اسمه الخالق البارئ المصور : فيرقى من المخلوق إلى الخالق ، وينتقل من ملاحظة المصنوع إلى ملاحظة الصانع ؛ حتى يصير بحيث كلما نظر إلى شيء وجد اللّه عنده .
pairs.en: Then, in the chapter on God's names, explaining the name “God”: “Every possible thing has no existence [of its own]; rather its existence is from the aspect (*jiha*) through which it faces the Necessary, exalted is He.” This is indicated by the words “Everything except God is vain.” In explaining the names “the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner”: “He ascends from the created to the Creator and passes from contemplation of the product to contemplation of its Maker, until he reaches the point that whenever he looks at anything he finds God with it.”

editorial_note: The phrase «بهذا الاعتبار» is decisive: the hadith description is being explained *under this consideration*, tied to the aspirant’s attainment. The phrase “the thing has no existence” is immediately followed by the qualifier that its being is from the aspect by which it faces the Necessary; it should not be decontextualized as a denial of all created actuality. The al-Samarqandī quotation is a separate, reported triad and cannot simply be turned into a binding Sunni legal classification of those who notice created causes.

title: Neither indwelling nor crude separateness
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī quoting and discussing earlier authorities; follow explicit attribution in each paragraph

pairs.ar: وفي شرح اسمه الحفيظ : حظ العارف خصوصا أن يعرف باطنه عن ملاحظة الأغيار ، وظاهره عن موافقة الفجار . وفي شرح اسمه الحق : وحظ العبد فيه أن يرى اللّه حقّا ، وما سواه باطلا في ذاته ، حقّا بإيجاده واختراعه . وفي شرح اسمه النور : الظاهر لنفسه ، المظهر لغيره ، ولا شك في أن الوجود إذا قوبل بالعدم كان الظهور للوجود والخفاء للعدم ، ولما كان الباريء تعالى موجودا بذاته مبرّأ عن ظلمة العدم وإمكان طروّه ، وكان وجود سائر الأشياء فائضا عن وجوده ؛ صح إطلاق اسم النور عليه ، إلى غير ذلك من المواضع .
pairs.en: In explaining the name “the Preserver” (*al-Ḥafīẓ*): “The share of the knower, in particular, is to protect his inwardness from looking to others, and his outwardness from acting as wrongdoers act.” On “the Real” (*al-Ḥaqq*): “The servant's share is to see God as real, and everything else as unreal *in itself*, yet real through His bringing it into being and originating it.” On “the Light”: “That which is manifest in itself and renders other things manifest. There is no doubt that when being is set in opposition to nonbeing, manifestation belongs to being and hiddenness to nonbeing. Since the Creator, exalted is He, exists through Himself, free of the darkness of nonbeing and even the possibility of its overtaking Him, whereas the being of all other things flows forth from His being, it is correct to apply the name ‘Light’ to Him.” Similar examples occur elsewhere.

pairs.ar: ومنها ما قال الفاضل المحقق شرف الدين الطيبي ، بعد نقله ما نقلناه عن الواحدي والبغوي عن « وهب » : وهذا لا يدل على لزوم الجسمية ، وكذلك القرب ، وذكر سائر ما نقلناه عن القاضي في شرح المشكاة ، في تلك المواضع . وقال في أسماء اللّه تعالى وإحصاء الأخص له : أن يستغرق قلبه باللّه تعالى ، ولا يلتفت إلى أحد سواه ، ولا يرجو ولا يخاف فيما يأتي يذر إلا إياه ؛ لأنه هو الحق الثابت وما عداه باطل ، قال اللّه تعالى : كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُ [ القصص : 88 ] .
pairs.en: Another authority is the learned verifier Sharaf al-Dīn al-Ṭībī. After citing the account from Wahb which we transmitted from al-Wāḥidī and al-Baghawī, he writes: “This does not require corporeality, nor does [such] nearness.” He also cited, at those places in his commentary on *al-Mishkāt*, the other material which we related from the judge. Concerning the names of God and the most distinctive way to enumerate them, he says that one should “fill the heart with God, attend to none besides Him, and hope in or fear none besides Him in whatever one does or leaves undone, for He is the unshakably Real while everything else is vain. God says: ‘Everything perishes but His Face’” (Q 28:88).

pairs.ar: وفي شرح اسمه البصير نقل عن سهل ، أنه قال منذ كذا سنة : إنما أخاطب الحق تعالى والناس يتوهمون إني أكلمهم ، وفي معناه أنشد : وظنّوني أخاطبهم قديما * وأنت بما أخاطبهم مرادي هذه صفة الجمع التي أشار إليها القوم . وفي شرح اسمه الواحد الأحد : وحظ العبد أن يغوص لجة التوحيد ، ويستغرق فيه ، حتى لا يرى من الأزل إلى الأبد غير الواحد الأحد ، إلى غير ذلك من المواضع .
pairs.en: Explaining the name “the All-Seeing,” he relates from Sahl, who said: “For so many years I have addressed none but the Real, exalted is He, while people have thought I was speaking to them.” Someone versified the same meaning: “They thought I had long been addressing them, / while You were the One I intended through my words to them.” This is the attribute of gathering (*jamʿ*) to which the people of the path have referred. In explaining the names “the One, the Unique,” he says: “The servant's share is to plunge into the ocean depths of unity and become absorbed therein, until from beginningless eternity to endless eternity he sees none but the One, the Unique.”

pairs.ar: ومنها ما قال الفاضل المحقق سراج الدين - صاحب كشف الكشاف - في ديباجته : الحمد للّه الذي أنار الأعيان بنور الوجود ، وجعلها مرائي صفاته ، واختار منها نوع الإنسان لجمعه سر الأكوان ، فكمل مجالي ذاته . وفي قوله تعالى : فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ اللَّهِ [ البقرة : 115 ] ، أنه تمهيد في ذكر نفي الولد ؛ لأن من له الجهات كلها يتعالى عنها ، فيستحيل أن يماثله ذو جهة ، والولد من جنس الوالد
pairs.en: Another is the learned verifier Sirāj al-Dīn, author of *Kashf al-Kashshāf*, who writes in his preface: “Praise belongs to God, who illumined the entities with the light of being and made them mirrors of His attributes, and chose from among them the human species because it comprehends the secret of the worlds, thereby perfecting the places in which His Essence appears.” On “There is the Face of God” (Q 2:115), he says that it prepares the way for the denial of divine offspring, because He to whom all directions belong is exalted beyond them; consequently no entity bounded by a direction can resemble Him, whereas offspring is of the same kind as its parent ... [continues on p. 38].

editorial_note: The al-Bayḍāwī passage states both «باطلا في ذاته» and «حقّا بإيجاده واختراعه», expressly indicating one judgement under the thing’s own aspect and another under divine production. Both clauses are crucial. The Ṭībī passage expressly rejects a corporealist reading of divine closeness. The precise identification of *Kashf al-Kashshāf* and its authorship should be checked.

title: Completion of twelve transmitted authorities and epistemic reticence
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī quoting and discussing earlier authorities; follow explicit attribution in each paragraph

pairs.ar: لا محالة . وفي قوله تعالى : أَ وَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ [ فصلت : 53 ] فمن شهده ؛ شهد كل شيء . ثم في قوله : وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْباطِنُ [ الحديد : 3 ] ، وهو الظاهر بوجوده ؛ لأن كل الموجودات بظهوره ظاهرة ، الباطن بكنهه ، إلى غير ذلك من المواضع .
pairs.en: ... necessarily. On “Is it not enough that your Lord is witness over every thing?” (Q 41:53), he says: “Whoever witnesses Him witnesses everything.” On “The Outward and the Inward” (Q 57:3), He is “Outward through His being, for all existents are manifest through His manifestation, and Inward through His innermost reality.” There are many similar places.

pairs.ar: فهؤلاء الاثني عشر أئمة أطبقوا على قبولها ، ووقع في كلام بعضهم النقل عن هؤلاء الكبار ، كالحسن بن علي ، وابن عباس ، وابن عمر ، وجعفر ، وأبي فارس ، ويوسف بن الحسين ، وعامر بن قيس ، الواسطي ، وأبي بكر الفارسي ، والنهرجوري ، وأبي عثمان الحيري ، والقاسم ، ومحمد بن واسع ، وابن عطاء ، ورويم ، والخراز ، والنصر آبادي ، وأبي على الدقاق بالتصريح ، وعن غيرهم بالتلويح .
pairs.en: **Al-Mahāʾimī resumes his own synthesis:** These twelve leading authorities agreed in accepting these [truths], and in the words of some there are explicit transmissions from these great figures: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Jaʿfar, Abū Fāris, Yūsuf ibn al-Ḥusayn, ʿĀmir ibn Qays, al-Wāsiṭī, Abū Bakr al-Fārisī, al-Nahrajūrī, Abū ʿUthmān al-Ḥīrī, al-Qāsim, Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ, Ibn ʿAṭāʾ, Ruwaym, al-Kharrāz, al-Naṣrābādhī and Abū ʿAlī al-Daqqāq; and there are implicit references to others.

pairs.ar: ونقل الشيخ أبو طالب المكي والغزالي ، عن ابن عباس : « لو فسرت هذه الآية اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ وَمِنَ الْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ [ الطلاق : 12 ] ؛ لرجمتموني » « 1 » .
pairs.en: Shaykh Abū Ṭālib al-Makkī and al-Ghazālī also transmit from Ibn ʿAbbās: “If I explained this verse—‘God it is who created seven heavens and of the earth their like’ (Q 65:12)—you would stone me.”

pairs.ar: ونقل الغزالي منهاج العابدين عن الإمام زين العابدين : إنّي لأكتم من علمي جواهره * كي لا يرى الحقّ ذو الجهل فيقتتنا وقد تقدّم في هذا أبو حسن * إلى الحسين وأوصى قبله للمناء يا ربّ جوهر علم لو أبوح به * لقيل أنت ممّن يعبد الوثنا ولاستحلّ رجال جاهلون دمي * يرون أقبح ما يأتونه حسنا وقد روي البخاري ، عن أبي هريرة : « حفظت من رسول اللّه صلى اللّه عليه وسلم وعاءين من العلم ، فأما أحدهما فبثثته ، وأما الآخر لو بثثته لقطع مني هذا البلعوم » « 2 » . فتأمل هذه الجملة ترشد إن شاء اللّه تعالى .
pairs.en: Al-Ghazālī, in *Minhāj al-ʿābidīn*, transmits from Imām Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn: “I conceal the jewels of my knowledge, / lest an ignorant person see the truth and bring ruin upon us. / Abū Ḥasan was before me in this, / and entrusted [it] to al-Ḥusayn, while before him [the reading is corrupt]. / O many a jewel of knowledge which, if I revealed it, / people would say, ‘You are one who worships idols!’ / Ignorant men would deem it lawful to spill my blood, / thinking the ugliest of their actions beautiful.” Al-Bukhārī also relates from Abū Hurayra: “I preserved two vessels of knowledge from the Messenger of God, peace be upon him. One I disseminated; as for the other, if I disseminated it, this throat of mine would be cut.” Reflect upon this collection of testimonies and you will, God willing, receive guidance.

editorial_note: The printed poetry has unstable wording, especially «للمَنَاء» and the second verse. Do not assign its attribution to Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn with historical certainty before checking its transmission. The Abū Hurayra report is a distinct ḥadīth, not proof that the earlier poems share its authority. This page ends chapter 1; chapter 2 starts p. 39.

title: Why rational demonstrations are offered after transmitted testimony
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī (argument, with occasional cited authorities)

pairs.ar: الفصل الثاني في البراهين العقلية على وجود الواجب اعلم أن جمهور العارفين اقتصروا على الأدلة الكشفية ، أي الضرورية الوجدانية ؛ لرفع الحجب الظلمانية ، وبالمجاهدة التي مقدمة الهداية في قوله عزّ وجل : وَالَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا فِينا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنا [ العنكبوت : 69 ] ، وبالتقوى : وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ اللَّهُ [ البقرة : 282 ] ، وبكمال التوجه إلى اللّه تعالى ، ولم يرتبوا المقدمات النظرية ؛ لما أنها توقع أهلها في الحيرة المذمومة بإثارة الشبهات المظلمة ؛ إلا من عصمه اللّه بالقوة القدسية والملكات الملكية ، المؤيدة للقوة الحدسية ؛ إلا أن العامة لما بالغوا في الإنكار عليها ، وزعموا أن فيها القطع ببطلان جميع الأحكام - العقلية والحسية والفطرية الغريزية - عقيب المجاهدات الجزافية ؛ فمنشأها استحكام سوء المزاج في موضوعات القوة النفسانية ، وإحراق المواد الصالحة المثيرة للوساوس الخيالية ، واستيلاء المرّة السوداوية ، وغلبة الجنون والمياليخوليا ، وكان ذلك موقعا لهم في الشرك الخفي ، وسببا لخوف سوء الخاتمة ، كما نقله الغزالي عن بعض العارفين ، ودل الحديث النبوي على أنهم أهل العزة باللّه ؛ وجب إيراد تلك المقدمات ورفع ما يستدرجهم من الشبهات ؛ لعلهم يقفون عن الإنكار ، أو ينقلبون إلى الإبصار .
pairs.en: **Chapter Two: Rational demonstrations for the existence of the Necessary Existent.** Know that most of the knowers have confined themselves to proofs furnished by unveiling—that is, immediate, inwardly experienced certainties—for the removal of darkening veils. They proceed through spiritual striving, which precedes guidance in the divine saying, “Those who strive in Us, We shall surely guide them to Our ways” (Q 29:69), through Godfearingness—“Fear God, and God teaches you” (Q 2:282)—and through complete turning towards God. They have not set out discursive premises, because these can plunge their practitioners into blameworthy perplexity through the generation of darkening doubts, except for someone whom God protects by a holy faculty and angelic dispositions supporting the faculty of immediate intuition. But ordinary people have gone to extremes in denouncing these knowers. They allege that the latter, following arbitrary spiritual struggles, categorically reject every judgement—rational, sensory, innate and instinctive—and that the cause is a deeply ingrained disturbance of temperament affecting the seats of the psychic faculties, the consumption of healthy bodily materials giving rise to imaginative obsessions, the predominance of black bile, and the mastery of madness and melancholy. Such an accusation exposes its proponents to hidden associationism and to the fear of an evil end, as al-Ghazālī relates from certain knowers; a Prophetic report, meanwhile, indicates that these people possess honour through God. Therefore it becomes necessary to set forth the [rational] premises and dispel the doubts that entrap the critics, in the hope that they will cease their denial—or be transformed into people who see.

pairs.ar: فنقول : هاهنا مقامان : أحدهما في تحقق الوجود المطلق ، والثاني وجوبه بالذات . المقام الأول : اعلم أن تحقق الوجود عن الأفكار أظهر من تحقق النور الحسي عند الإبصار ؛ لكن شدة ظهوره عكست فيه الأمر إلى ضده ، كما أن نور الشمس لما بلغ غاية الإشراق ؛ ظن بعض الخلائق أنه ليس وراء الألوان شيء وراءه ؛ لكن غروب الشمس ظل ضروريا بين محل الظل وموقع الضياء ، وليس كذلك الوجود الذي هو نور الأنوار ؛ لدوام حضوره مع الأشياء على نسق واحد ، فأنكر كثير من مهرة النظار تحققه في الخارج ، وزعموا أن ليس فيه إلا الماهيات ، وإنما هو من المعقولات الثانية والاعتبارات العقلية المحضة ، وكل ذلك لكون النهاية تشبه البداية ؛ لا متناع التحقق ورائها وامتناعه دونها ، والامتناعان يتحدان في تحققه ويختلفان في النسبة ، فلم يكن بد من كشف ما اشتبه عليهم .
pairs.en: We say that there are two questions here: first, the actuality of unrestricted existence (*al-wujūd al-muṭlaq*); second, its being necessary through itself. **First question.** Know that the actuality of existence is more evident to thought than the actuality of sensible light is to sight. Yet its very intensity of manifestation has made things seem the opposite of what they are. In the same way, because sunlight reaches the extreme of radiance, some people have imagined that nothing lies beyond colours; but sunset necessarily brings out the distinction between places of shadow and illumination. Existence, the light of lights, is not like this: it remains constantly present with things in one and the same manner. Hence many highly skilled speculative thinkers deny its extramental actuality, claiming that nothing exists outside the mind except quiddities and that existence itself is only a second intelligible or purely mental consideration. This results from the likeness between the furthest limit and the starting point: actuality is impossible beyond the former and impossible short of the latter. These two impossibilities are alike in their [relation to] actuality, though different in the relations intended. It is therefore necessary to expose the source of the confusion.

editorial_note: The final contrast of two impossibilities («الامتناعان») is obscure in this transcription. “More evident to thought” renders the recorded «عن الأفكار» provisionally; a printed witness must be consulted. **Online page:** https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9637/39?lang=ar

title: Existence is not a merely mental consideration: objections and replies
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī (argument, with occasional cited authorities)

pairs.ar: فنقول : لا شك أن لكل ماهية وجدت تحققا مطلقا ، فالتحقق إما عينه أو جزؤه ، فظاهر ؛ لأنه لا يكون مجرد أمر اعتباري ، وإما زائد ، فلا شك أن قوام التحقق المقيد ضرورة أن الضد وصف لا يقوم بذاته ، فأما أن يقوم بالتحقق المطلق أو المقيد والثاني بين البطلان ؛ فتعيّن الأول وما به قوام المحقق أولى بأن يكون محققا ، وإن كان القيد اعتباريا فالمتحقق هو المطلق ، وإن كان منع ثبوت التحقق للماهية ؛ كانت الخارجية عين الذهنية ؛ إذ الذهني أولى بأن يكون اعتباريا .
pairs.en: We say: there is no doubt that every quiddity which exists possesses actuality unrestrictedly considered. This actuality is either identical with the quiddity, a part of it, or something additional. In either of the first two cases it is evident that actuality cannot be a merely conceptual affair. If it is additional, the determinate actuality must have something by which it subsists, since a description cannot subsist through itself. It must subsist either through unrestricted actuality or through determinate actuality; the second alternative is plainly untenable, so the first is established. That by which something actual subsists has an even stronger claim to be actual. If the restriction is merely conceptual, the actual reality is what is unrestricted. If the attribution of actuality to quiddity is denied, extramental existence would be identical to existence in the mind—for mental existence would be even more liable to be called conceptual.

pairs.ar: على أن التحقق لو كان اعتباريا ؛ فالكل اعتباري ، حتى المعتبر على أن ثبوته مدرك بالضرورة ، فمنعه مكابرة . قيل لو ثبت لكل ماهية تحقق لكان لنسبته إليها تحقق ، وبينها نسبة محققة وتسلسل . قلنا : إن لم تكن موجودة ، فظاهر وإن كانت ، فالنسبة الثانية عين حصوله لها . قيل : إن ثبت لها فصفة لا تستقل ، وإلا تتأخر لثبوتها ، فلا يثبت لها ، ثم أن يكون كيفية يتقدم عليها محلها ويصير أعم منه ؛ على أنه حين إذ يقوم بها فيفتقر إليها .
pairs.en: Moreover, were actuality merely conceptual, everything—including the person making the conceptual consideration—would be merely conceptual; yet its reality is grasped immediately, and denying it is obstinate disputation. **Objection:** If every quiddity possesses an actuality, then its relation to that actuality must itself be actual, and another actual relation must link them, producing an infinite regress. **Reply:** If the relation does not itself exist [in the stipulated manner], the answer is evident; if it does, the second relation is precisely actuality's belonging to the quiddity. **Objection:** If actuality is affirmed as belonging to it, it is a nonsubsistent attribute; otherwise [its attribution] would be postponed until after the quiddity's own establishment, and it could not be established of it. It would furthermore be a quality whose subject precedes it and is more general than it; thus actuality would inhere in that subject and depend upon it.

pairs.ar: قلنا : ما ليس بجوهر قد لا يكون عرضا ، والكيفية عرض ، فليس معنى القيام الافتقار ، فإن الصورة لا تفتقر إلى الهيولي . قيل : تحقق الحادث المعدوم الآن ليس بحاصل ؛ وإلا تحقق حين لا تحقق له ، فإذا حصل يقال حصل تحققه بعد ما لم يكن ، فالتحقق من حيث هو غير حاصل . قلنا : ليس بحاصلة ، وهي حاصلة لنفسه ، والإلزام سلب الشيء عن نفسه ، والحاصل بعد ما لم تكن مقارنته . قيل : تحقق الماهية ثابتة ، فلو ثبت المطلق تعدد في ما وجد ، وفيه تحصيل الحاصل .
pairs.en: **Reply:** Not everything which is not a substance is thereby an accident, whereas quality is an accident. Nor does ‘subsisting’ invariably mean ‘depending’; substantial form, for example, does not depend on prime matter [in the sense intended by the argument]. **Objection:** The actuality of a newly originated thing that is now nonexistent is not present. Otherwise actuality would obtain when the thing had none. When it later comes to be we say that its actuality has arisen after not existing; consequently actuality as such was absent. **Reply:** [The quiddity] is not actual, but actuality is actual through itself; the proposed consequence deprives a thing of itself. What comes about after not having been there is the conjunction [of actuality with the quiddity]. **Objection:** The quiddity's actuality is already established; if unrestricted actuality also existed, there would be a duplication in what exists, an idle obtaining of what is already obtained.

pairs.ar: قلنا : إن أريد بتحقق الماهية امتيازها ؛ فظاهر أن التحقق واحد ، وإن أريد موجوداتها ؛ فهي للماهية بالوجود ، وله بنفسه ؛ على أن التكرار إنما هو بالنسبة إلى أمر واحد ، وهنا أمران . قيل : يصدق على الاعتبارين ، ويمتنع كونها جزئيات جزئيات الحقيقي . قلنا : إذا كان في الخارج والصادق عليهما وهمي . قيل : لو كان حقيقيّا تكثر الواحد ؛ لأن تحقق الشيء في نفسه غير تحققه في مكانه أو زمانه أو حاله .
pairs.en: **Reply:** If the quiddity's actuality means its distinctness, it is clear that actuality is one. If its [actual] existents are intended, they belong to the quiddity by existence, while existence belongs to itself through itself. In any case repetition would concern one and the same matter, whereas two considerations are at issue here. **Objection:** It is predicable under both considerations, while it cannot be a genuine particular [under each]. **Reply:** [The transcribed wording here is syntactically insecure: the answer contrasts what is extramental with a merely imagined common predicate.] **Objection:** If actuality were real it would multiply what is one, since the actuality of a thing in itself differs from its actuality in a place, a time, or a state.

editorial_note: At least two readings are defective: «الضد وصف» may not be the intended noun, and the last objection and reply around «جزئيات جزئيات الحقيقي» are corrupt. The source text is preserved rather than silently normalised. **Online page:** https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9637/40?lang=ar

title: Relations do not multiply reality; first proof of necessary existence
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī (argument, with occasional cited authorities)

pairs.ar: قلنا : ممنوع ، وإنما تكثر الإضافات . قيل : لو تعين بنفسه انحصر في الواحد والكثرة مشاهدة ما هو كلي ، لا يفيد ضمّه جزئية الماهية الكلية ، فيتحقق في الخارج ، فهو كسائر الكليات الاعتبارية ، فلا بدّ لتحققها من انضمام التعين أو ملزومها إليها ، فهو الوجود العيني لها ، والتعين اعتباري ؛ لأنه انضمام المشخص وهو ذهني ؛ إذ لو كان خارجيّا لم يضم إلى الماهية الذهنية الكلية في الخارج ، وكذا ملزومه ؛ لأن الاعتباري لا يلزم الحقيقي ، وإلا امتنع تحققه بدون اعتباره ، والحقيقي متحقق بدون المعتبر .
pairs.en: **Reply:** We deny [that its own actuality multiplies it]; it is only the relations which multiply. **Objection:** If existence is determinate by itself, it would be confined to one, whereas multiplicity is witnessed. Moreover what is universal cannot become a real particular outside the mind simply by adjoining it to a universal quiddity. It is like the other conceptual universals: its extramental realization would require the addition either of determination or of something necessarily connected with determination. But determination is conceptual, being the joining of an individuating feature; that joining is mental, since an extramental thing could not be added, *outside the mind*, to a universal quiddity which exists in the mind. The same holds for its necessary concomitant: a conceptual consideration cannot entail a real thing, for otherwise reality could not exist without someone's considering it, whereas real things obtain without the person making the consideration.

pairs.ar: قلنا : متعين بنفسه ، والتكثر إنما هو للماهيات وتعينها ؛ إما بنفسها بشرط اتصافها بالوجود ، أو بأسباب خارجية ، وإن لم يتعين بنفسه ؛ فيجوز أن يكون العيني لها طبيعة متعينة ، أو من حيث هي من الكلي والجزئي ، لا نفس التعين ولا ملزومه . المقام الثاني : فيه طرق : الطريق الأول : إن الوجود المشترك بالمعنى بين كل موجود بالذات لا يقبل العدم ، فمطلقه المحيط واجب .
pairs.en: **Reply:** Existence is determinate through itself; plurality belongs to quiddities, and their particularization is either through themselves on condition of their being qualified by existence or through extrinsic causes. Even were existence not determinate through itself, their extramental existence could be a determinate nature, or a nature considered apart from the alternatives universal and particular; it need not be determination itself, nor its concomitant. **Second question: the ways of proving intrinsic necessity. First way:** Existence, whose meaning is shared by everything that exists through itself, cannot receive nonexistence; therefore the unrestricted and all-encompassing reality of existence is necessary.

pairs.ar: أما الاشتراك فيه فبديهي ، ولو عند تصوره بالوجه أو بالفكر ؛ لكن لغاية وضوحه اشتبه أمره ، فجعل عين الماهيات ، فتنبه بأنه يبقى اعتقاد الوجود مع زوال اعتقاد الخصوصيات . قيل : يزول اعتقاد وجود خصوصية بوجود أخرى ، فأين يبقى المشترك بينهما ؟ قلنا : نحن نجد أن متعلق اعتقاد الباقي هو معنى الوجود - وإن لم يوضع له لفظ قط . قيل : لا يزول اعتقاد وجود الشيء لو اعتقد أنه نفس الوجود ، ثم أنه جوهر ، ثم أنه عرض فلا ، فللوجود وجود ويتسلسل .
pairs.en: That such a common meaning is present is self-evident, even if we conceive it only under an aspect or through thought. Yet its extreme clarity has led to confusion, and it has been taken to be identical with quiddities. Notice that the conviction that there is existence remains even when our convictions concerning particular specifications pass away. **Objection:** The belief that one particular thing exists disappears when the existence of another is affirmed; where, then, does the common element remain? **Reply:** We discover that what remains the object of our conviction is the meaning of existence—even if no word had ever been coined for it. **Objection:** If one believes that a thing is existence itself, that it is a substance, then that it is an accident, the belief does not persist in the proposed way; and existence itself must have existence, prompting an infinite regress.

pairs.ar: قلنا : الوجود عينه في الحقيقة ، غيره بالاعتبار ، وينقطع التسلسل بقطعه ، وكونه زائدا في صورة ، لا يستلزم زيادته في أخرى . قيل : فيشترك بين نفسه وغيره . قلنا : يلغي المغايرة الاعتبارية ، وأيضا أن الوجود ينقسم إلى واجب وممكن ، والمورد مشترك . قيل : الاشتراك لفظي ، وجاز العالم إما ممكن أو واجب ، والمورد نفسه الماهية .
pairs.en: **Reply:** Existence is in reality identical with itself; it differs from it only by conceptual consideration. Once that consideration is removed the regress stops. That existence is additional in one case does not entail that it must be additional in another. **Objection:** Then it would be shared between itself and something other than itself. **Reply:** The difference established solely through consideration drops away. Moreover, existence is divided into necessary and possible, and what receives that division is common to both. **Objection:** The sharing might be merely verbal; and one may divide a [given] world into ‘possible’ or ‘necessary’ while what receives the division is its quiddity itself.

editorial_note: Do not read the common meaning of existence alone as an independent proof of one numerical extramental subject; the author adds ontological premises. The last objector wording is insecure. **Online page:** https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9637/41?lang=ar

title: Further replies on common existence and nonexistence
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī (argument, with occasional cited authorities)

pairs.ar: قلنا : قسمته عقلية لا تتوقف على وضع تعليليه معا ، بأن وجوده إن حصل من ذاته فواجب ، أو من غيره فممكن ، ومنع التعليل بتقدير عينية الوجود ؛ لامتناع أن يقال الهوية الخاصة إن اقتضت نفسها لذاتها فواجبة ، وإلا فممكنة ؛ إذ لا معنى له مكابرة لصحته بالضرورة ، والماهية المطلقة ، إنما تنقسم بانضمام مقسم ، فإن ضم إليها الوجود فلا بدّ من بقائه مع قسيمها ، وهو استمرار الوجود ، فاشتراكه يستلزم الوجود ، ولا ينقصان بالماهية والشخص لاشتراك مطلقيهما ، وأيضا بأن الشيء ينحصر في الموجود والمعدوم ، والعدم عام ، فكذا مقابله ، وإلا انحصر بين عام وخاص .
pairs.en: **Reply:** It is a rational division, which does not depend upon our affirming both alternatives as actual: if a thing's existence proceeds from itself it is necessary; if from another, it is possible. To deny the explanatory distinction on the supposition that existence is identical with the thing—because one allegedly cannot say that a particular identity, if it entails itself through itself, is necessary, while otherwise it is possible—is sheer obstinacy: the statement is necessarily intelligible. An unrestricted quiddity is divided only by adding a dividing feature. If existence is added to it, existence must remain with each opposing member of the division; the continued presence of existence is precisely the common element. This sharing entails a common existence and is not undone by appeal to quiddity or individuality, since those notions too possess their unrestricted meanings. Further, anything is either existent or nonexistent. Nonexistence is general, and so must its opposite be; otherwise the exhaustive alternatives would be a general and a particular.

pairs.ar: قيل : رفع هوية خاصة والحصر بينه وبين ثبوتها . قلنا : يفهم الجمهور العموم ، لا يقال : إن وجد الرفع العام في سائر الهويات اجتمع فيه النقيضان ؛ وإلا امتنع صدق رفع شيء غير تلك الهوية ؛ لأنا نقول : هو ، وإن كان علما بحسب الهويات ؛ لكن لا تتحقق له من حيث هو ، بل بشيء من الإضافات ، وعورضت هذه الشبهات بأدلة عينية وجود للماهيات ، فمنها إن زاد فالماهيات من حيث هي معدومة ، فيلزم اتصاف الموجود بالمعدوم .
pairs.en: **Objection:** What is negated is only a particular identity, and the exhaustive distinction is between its being and its removal. **Reply:** Ordinary understanding takes the expression universally. One should not object that, if this general negation obtains among other identities, contradictories would be joined; if not, it would be impossible to affirm the negation of anything besides that identity. For though the expression is differentiated according to the identities, as such it is not actual except through certain relations. These doubts have also been confronted with alleged proofs that existence is identical with quiddities. One such proof says: if existence were additional, quiddities as such would be nonexistent, so an existent would be qualified by nonexistence.

pairs.ar: قلنا : من حيث هي لا تتصف بهما ، بل ينضمان إليها انضمام السواد والبياض بالجسم ، ومنها أن الصفة الثبوتية للشيء فرع ثبوته في نفسه بالضرورة ، فيكون لها قبل وجودها وجود ، فيتقدم على نفسه ويتسلسل . قلنا : الضرورة في صفة وجودية هي غير الوجود ، ومنها لو زاد لكان وجودا . قلنا : ثبوت الشيء لنفسه ليس أمرا زائدا عليه ، وأما امتناع العدم على الوجود ، هو أيضا بديهي ؛ لكن لما ذكر نبه عليه بأن قبوله العدم إما لعروضه له فيلزم اتصاف أحد النقيضين بالآخر ، أو لا فيلزم انقلاب طبيعة إلى طبيعة أخرى ، وبطلانها ضروري .
pairs.en: **Reply:** Quiddities considered in themselves are characterised by neither existence nor nonexistence. These are joined to them as blackness or whiteness may be joined to a body. **Another objection:** Every positive attribute of a thing presupposes that thing's own establishment. Existence would therefore need an existence prior to its own existence, producing self-priority and an infinite regress. **Reply:** That principle of presupposition applies to a positive attribute which is *other than existence*. **Another objection:** If existence were additional, it would itself require existence. **Reply:** A thing's being established as itself is not something additional to it. That nonexistence cannot befall existence is likewise self-evident; the preceding argument serves to bring this out. Nonexistence would either befall existence as an accident—in which case one contradictory would be qualified by its opposite—or else existence would turn into a different nature. Both are necessarily impossible.

pairs.ar: قيل : المراد إمكان انتفائه . قلنا : امتنع إمكان كون الانتفاء ؛ لامتناع كون المحال ممكنا . قيل : لا يمتنع اتصاف أحد النقيضين بالآخر ؛ وإنما الممتنع حمل أحدهما على الآخر ، بل خارجا عنه قابلا له ولما يقابله ، فامتناع ثبوته لنفسه مع امتناع قبولها له ولمّا يقابلها ؛ أظهر وأجل ، فإنه إذا امتنع مثلا حمل الأسود على ذات الأسود القابلة للسواد ، فامتناع ثبوته لنفس الأسود أولى ؛ على أن منع استحالة اتصاف أحد النقيضين بالآخر مكابرة .
pairs.en: **Objection:** The intended meaning is only that existence might cease. **Reply:** Such cessation cannot even be possible, because an impossibility cannot be possible. **Objection:** It is not impossible for one of two contradictories to qualify the other; what is impossible is to predicate the one of the other, rather than of a subject outside both which can receive either. **Reply:** [The syntax of this rebuttal is unstable in the transcription.] The impossibility of a contradictory's being predicated of itself in the proposed manner is still more evident: for example, if blackness cannot be predicated of the very subject considered as the recipient of blackness, then predicating it of blackness itself would be still more problematic. At any rate, denying that a thing can be qualified by its contradictory is mere obstinacy.

editorial_note: Several clauses, particularly the final dialectic about subject and blackness, are transmitted in doubtful syntax and need photographic verification. The translation follows the visible argumentative direction without claiming textual certainty. **Online page:** https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9637/42?lang=ar

title: Real unity, names, and the possible objection from a specially necessary nature
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī (argument, with occasional cited authorities)

pairs.ar: قيل : الاشتراك يستلزم العموم المنافي للوجود لا متناعه في الخارج ، ويستلزم الأفراد المنافية للتوحيد . قلنا : ما يقال عليه ليس من الأفراد ، بل الكل واحد واجب بالذات كثير بصفات ممكنة زائدة على الذات ، فاشتراكه باعتبار إضافته إلى الماهيات ، وتعدده باعتبار ظهوره فيها ، فليس عاما لتحققه ضرورة تحقق الكل به ، ولا خاصّا بقيد اعتباري كالتجرد عن الماهية ؛ وإلا قبل العدم عند عدم اعتباره ، ولا يقيد وجودي ؛ لأنه إن كان كالصورة تركب الواجب ، أو كالفرض فلا يكون لازما لنفس طبيعته ؛ لامتناع تقيد الشيء به كنفسه لوجوده ؛ حيث يوجد الشيء فهو عام فيعم القيد أيضا ، فيكون مقارنا ، فيستند إلى مباين ؛ إذ لو استند إلى لازم لزم القيد ، فيكون مفارقا ، ولزم التسلسل في الأمور المترتبة بين حاصرين الذات والقيد ، والقيد المحض .
pairs.en: **Objection:** Sharing entails universality, which is incompatible with real existence because a universal cannot exist outside the mind; it also entails multiple instances, which contradict divine oneness. **Reply:** What the term is predicated of is not a collection of independently existing instances. Rather the whole is one, necessary through itself, while plurality occurs through possible attributes additional to the Essence. Sharing is considered with respect to its relations to quiddities, and multiplicity with respect to its appearance within them. Thus it is not universal in the manner alleged, since all things are necessarily actual through it. Nor is it a particular marked by a merely conceptual limitation, such as being disengaged from quiddity: otherwise, when that limitation ceased to be considered, existence itself would become susceptible to nonexistence. Neither can a positive restriction qualify it: if like a form, it would render the Necessary composite; if like a differentia, it would not be a necessary concomitant of the very nature of existence. The ensuing argument about a restriction's relation to its subject is compressed and textually uncertain, but its point is to reject a distinct real delimitation that would require another principle or an infinite regress.

pairs.ar: قيل : إنما لا يقبل المطلق العدم لو كان ذات المقيد ، وذلك باطل لصحة حمل المطلق عليه ، مع امتناع حمل أحد الذاتين على الأخرى ، فالحقيقة الواجبة طبيعة خاصة ملزومة للمطلق . قلنا : هي غير معقولة ؛ لأنها إن كانت ذات أفراد ذهنية ، فلو وجد منها فرد وامتنعت الباقية وكلها ممكنة ؛ فوجوب البعض وامتناع البواقي بالغير ؛ إذ ما بالذات لا يزال بالغير ، وإن لم تكن ذات إفراد ، فإن كانت مغايرة لحقيقة الوجود المطلق ، فلا تكون موجودة وإلا تركب مع الوجود ، فهي إما في ماهية حقيقة ، فيلزم قيام الوجود الواجب بها ، وهي غيره فتحتاج إلى الغير وتكون فاعلة له ، وإلا كان وجود الواجب من غيره .
pairs.en: **Objection:** Unrestricted existence could be immune to nonexistence only if it were the very essence of a determinate existent. But that is false: the unrestricted can be predicated of what is determinate, whereas one self-subsistent essence cannot be predicated of another. Necessary reality is therefore a special nature necessarily accompanied by unrestricted existence. **Reply:** Such a nature cannot be made intelligible. If it has instances in the mind, and one instance exists while the others are impossible, despite all being [conceptually] possible, the necessity of the former and impossibility of the latter must come from something extrinsic; for what belongs to something through itself is not eliminated by what comes from another. If the nature has no such instances and differs from unrestricted existence, it cannot itself be existent, lest it become a composite with existence. If it is a quiddity, necessary existence would subsist in it; but being other than existence, it would need what is other and would have to be the agent that brings existence about—otherwise the Necessary's existence would come from another.

pairs.ar: وقال أيضا : وعلة لوجوده فيتقدم عليه بالوجود ، على أنه لو جاز تأثيرها في تحققها ، جاز في تحقق العالم بلا وجود ، بأن تكون قبل الوجود علة حلولها في العقل الأول ثم لوجوده ، وكذا لما تحته من غير أن يحصل لها وجود فيسند إثبات وجود الصانع الواجب تعالى ، وجاز أيضا أن يكون ماهية كل شيء علة لوجوده من غير أن يؤثر فيه الواجب تعالى ؛ أما إذا كانت بسيطة فلأن ماهيته تعالى لما كانت بسيطة اقتضت وجودها ؛ فكذلك كل بسيط ، وأما إذا كانت مركبة ؛ فلأن ماهية الجزء والصورة والهيئة الاجتماعية يجوز كونها علة الاجتماع ، فيحصل ماهية المجموع ، وهي علة لوجود نفسها أو لوجود الأجزاء ،
pairs.en: It would also have to be the cause of its own existence and so precede itself in existence. Moreover, if such a quiddity could act to actualize itself, it could supposedly act to actualize the world without itself existing: before possessing existence it could cause its own inherence in the First Intellect and then the Intellect's existence, and similarly all subordinate things, without ever itself acquiring existence. Thus the proof of a necessary Creator would be undermined. It would also become admissible that the quiddity of every thing causes its own existence without the Necessary exerting any effect upon it. If simple, the argument would be that, just as the simple divine quiddity allegedly entails its own existence, so does every simple quiddity. If composite, the quiddity of the part, the form, and their composite arrangement could cause that arrangement, yielding the quiddity of the whole; this in turn could cause its own existence or that of its parts ...

editorial_note: The final paragraph continues on p.44. The compressed middle portion of the first reply is flagged; a translation must not silently smooth the corrupted source into a demonstrative syllogism. **Online page:** https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9637/43?lang=ar

title: Rejecting the specially necessary nature and intrinsic existential gradation
speaker_layer: al-Mahāʾimī (argument, with occasional cited authorities)

pairs.ar: وهي بشرط الإجماع فتصير علة لوجود نفسها أو لوجود الأجزاء ، وانعدام الحوادث ؛ لانعدام الشرائط والأمور المعدة التي يقتضي وجودها ، فتسقط أدلة وجود الواجب ؛ إما بشيء من الأمور العقلية التي لا تقبل الوجود ، فيلزم مع احتياج الواجب إلى الأمر العقلي ، وكونه قابلا وفاعلا وعلة للوجود - لا بشرط الوجود - أن يكون مبدأ الوجود العيني أمرا عقليّا يمتنع تحققه في الخارج ؛ فأنى يكون واجبا ملزوما للوجود ، وإذا لم تكن الطبيعة الملزومة مغايرة لحقيقة الوجود المطلق ؛ لزم امتناع استلزام الوجودات الممكنة للحقيقة المطلقة ، امتناع استلزامها للواجبة ، أو وجوب استلزام الوجودات الخاصة للمطلقة ، مع امتناع استلزام حقائق الممكنات للواجبة .
pairs.en: ... when that combination is stipulated, and the composite then becomes a cause of its own existence or of the existence of its parts. Perishable things would cease because of the absence of the conditions and preparatory factors required for their occurrence. Proofs of a Necessary Existent would thereby collapse. [On the alternative] that the alleged necessary nature is a merely intelligible thing which cannot possess existence, the Necessary itself would depend upon an intelligible item, while that item would be both receiver and agent, the cause of existence without being required to exist. The principle of extramental existence would then be something mental incapable of extramental actuality. How could that be a Necessary Existent inseparably connected with existence? But if the nature held to entail existence does not differ from the reality of unrestricted existence, one must either deny that possible existences entail unrestricted existence as they fail to entail necessary existence, or require particular existences to entail unrestricted existence despite possible quiddities' failure to entail the Necessary.
